newsitem.title: USA: Cosbys consider suing National Enquirer.
newsitem.headline: Cosbys consider suing National Enquirer.

text.p: Bill Cosby and his wife Camille are considering suing a tabloid newspaper whose $100,000 reward offer led to the arrest of a suspect in the murder of their only son, the actor's spokesman said on Monday.

Spokesman David Brokaw said the Cosbys demanded the National Enquirer print a retraction of a story that the supermarket tabloid ran in February describing Camille Crosby as being sedated and on the verge of a nervous breakdown.

They were also angered by the Enquirer's reference in the same story to Shawn Jackson, the woman Cosby admitted to having sex with 22 years ago, as his "mistress," Brokaw said, and at the statement that Camille Cosby had hired "gunmen" to hunt down their son's killer.
David Perel, executive editor of the Enquirer, said the paper was standing by its story. "There is no way we're backing off the factual basis of our coverage," he said.

"We've reported the story accurately, and we feel we've contributed to a greater societal good by helping the Los Angeles Police Department solve what was believed to be an unsolvable murder. But we regret any pain we have inadvertently caused the family," he said in a telephone call with Reuters.
Ennis Cosby, a 27-year-old doctoral student, was shot to death while changing a tire on a Los Angeles street on Jan. 16.

Earlier this month police arrested Mikhail Markhasev, a Ukrainian emigre, on suspicion of his murder. Police said Markhasev, whose arraignment on murder charges was postponed until next Friday, was tracked down from a tip received by the Enquirer. The newspaper offered a reward of $100,000 for information leading to conviction of the murderer.

Brokaw said the Florida-based Enquirer recently replied to the Cosbys' letter demanding the retraction. "They have offered to address the situation, but we don't think (the offer) goes far enough," Brokaw said.

The Enquirer's letter, he said, did not "really address the fact that they out and out put falsehoods in (the article), and they minimised that fact that they had one of their writers on the phone with me on a daily basis ... but he never said, 'Hey, would you call this woman Bill Cosby was with a mistress? Was Mrs. Cosby about ready to be sedated into oblivion? Did Mrs. Cosby hire gunmen? They never checked with the Cosbys, they took egregious liberties."
Brokaw said he was unsure what the next step would be because the Cosbys were in South Africa and he had been unable to inform them of the Enquirer's letter.

Brokaw said a libel lawsuit against the paper was one of the steps being explored. "But it would be wrong to say the Cosbys are threatening to sue the Enquirer. It is just one of the things they are considering."
